questions.prompt: Why is 200 KB of JavaScript more expensive than 200 KB of image?

options.text: JavaScript must be parsed, compiled, and executed on the main thread, while an image is mostly just decoded
Images are always compressed and JavaScript never is
JavaScript downloads more slowly than images

questions.explanation: Byte-for-byte, JS costs more because after download it is parsed, compiled, and executed on the main thread — work that blocks interactivity — whereas an image is largely decoded and painted.

questions.prompt: Order the four cost stages a script goes through.

items.text: Execute (run it on the main thread)

questions.explanation: A script is downloaded, parsed, compiled, and executed. The last three are CPU work on the main thread — the part that's uniquely expensive about JavaScript.

questions.prompt: To load a module on demand at runtime (enabling code splitting) you use dynamic ____().
questions.explanation: Dynamic import() fetches a module at runtime, so heavy or rarely-used code can be split into a separate chunk loaded only when needed.

questions.prompt: Which techniques reduce the amount of JavaScript users must process? Select all that apply.

options.text: Code-split with dynamic import() so features load on demand
Import only the functions you use, not whole libraries
Ship a broad polyfill bundle to every browser

questions.explanation: Code splitting, tree shaking, and granular imports all ship less JS. Sending polyfills to modern browsers that don't need them adds wasted parse/execute cost.

questions.prompt: What does tree shaking require in order to work?

options.text: Static ES module import/export (and correct sideEffects metadata)
That all code be in one file

questions.explanation: Tree shaking analyzes static ES module imports/exports to safely drop unused code; dynamic require() and importing whole libraries can defeat it.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Break the bundle into chunks loaded on demand
Remove unused exports at build time
Code that adds a missing feature for old browsers
Re-running JS to make server-rendered HTML interactive

questions.explanation: Code splitting and tree shaking reduce shipped JS; polyfills add features for old browsers; hydration is main-thread work that can hurt INP.
